Compensation = [0.80 × min(Monthly Contract Energy, Availability Declaration) − (Actual Delivered + Forced Outage + Scheduled Outage + Force Majeure Energy)] × Purchase Rate for that Month. If result is negative, payment is zero. Establishes that if monthly en
In the wet season (peak months Ashadh–Kartik), NEA/LDC can withhold 10% of Contract Energy or Availability Declaration as a "Reserve Margin" with ZERO compensation to the IPP.

No clause in Article 10 exempts an IPP from AD penalties when the generation shortfall is caused by NEA/NLDC dispatch curtailment. The penalty formula applies irrespective of cause (aside from Force Majeure).
30-year take-or-pay: NEA is obligated to pay for 100% of Contracted Energy from COD. Schedule 3 provides up to 72 cumulative hours (3 days) of unpaid outage per year.

Why Nepal can experience wet-season electricity surplus and dry-season scarcity within the same hydro-dominated system.

Seasonal mismatch is the structural misalignment between Nepal's monsoon-peaking hydropower generation profile and its comparatively stable year-round electricity demand. It is the central problem of Nepal's RoR-dominated electricity system.

Nepal's rivers flood in monsoon (June–September) and shrink in winter (December–February). Its electricity demand stays roughly the same all year. So hydro plants produce too much in monsoon and too little in winter. This is not a drought or a shortage of dams

"Seasonal mismatch is a temporary drought problem." It is not. It is a structural property of RoR hydro in a monsoon climate, present every year. "More dams will solve it." More run-of-river dams increase monsoon surplus without changing the dry-season floor.

The three public labels used to distinguish flagship evidence pages, useful work in progress and concise registry entries.

The wiki uses three public maturity labels to distinguish flagship evidence pages, useful work in progress and concise registry entries. Maturity is an editorial and evidence-readiness label, not a confidence score for every claim on a page.

Maturity applies to the page. Confidence applies to a claim. A Verified Core page can contain a low-confidence or unresolved item if it labels it honestly; a Registry Record can contain a high-confidence identity fact while remaining narratively thin.

A flagship page on the wiki's core reading path. It has an explicit excerpt, dated review, source provenance, a visible caveat and bounded claims. Verified Core does not mean complete or certain; important gaps must remain visible.

A useful page with analysis or evidence that is still being reconciled, deepened or refreshed. It may contain strong individual claims, but the page as a whole has material gaps or does not yet meet the flagship review standard.

A concise structured record—often a project, organisation, place or dataset—whose basic identity or attributes are recorded. It may intentionally have little narrative. Registry Record must not be mistaken for a verified project status or complete dossier.
